generator.name: hand-authored (env/dungeon.js + DungeonDecor)
generator.note: fixed layout: the decor was built once and read back; nothing is random at load time

code.note: sha256 of the listed lab source files at export time; labCommit = lookdev-lab HEAD; uncommitted = listed files that differ from HEAD (the export used the working tree)

coordinateSystem.system: three.js right-handed, Y up, metres. x = east, z = south (the default game camera looks north), y = height above the ground datum (water level 0 unless the map says otherwise).
coordinateSystem.yaw: yawDeg = rotation about +Y in degrees, three.js Object3D.rotation.y (positive turns +z toward +x: a piece whose front is local +z faces (sin yaw, cos yaw): 0 = south, 90 = east, 180 = north, -90 = west).
coordinateSystem.note: WORLD coordinates. The crypt is centred at (-17, 0), the cave at (18, 0); the AREA-LOCAL coordinates of env/dungeon.js (areas.*.def, outline) are world minus the area centre

splat.note: world coordinates (the area centre is already added)
world coordinates (the area centre is already added)

heightfield.sample: cell centre: x = x0 + (i + 0.5) * cell, z = z0 + (j + 0.5) * cell (world coordinates); NaN = outside the outline + 0.45 m

outline.note: 480 samples at angle a = j / 480 * 2 pi (from +x toward +z): [wall radius m, wall height m], AREA-LOCAL coordinates (add the centre)

textures.decalsNote: 4 x 4 atlases, cell = row * 4 + col from the image top

vertexShade.note: grey vertex colour c = lerp(1, 0.06, smoothstep(y, 1.0, 2.28)) * (0.82 + 0.18 * smoothstep(y, 0.0, 0.4)), y = the vertex height in the lab GLB frame (metres, pivot at the bottom; module 2.283 m tall); multiply the base colour by it (material.vertexColors = true). The top of the wall fades to black (no ceiling: the room dissolves into darkness); lerp(a, b, t) = a + (b - a) t; smoothstep = THREE.MathUtils.smoothstep

dressing.note: everything the decor builds that is not a GLB: procedural meshes (three.js geometry type + parameters), other instanced groups, ground decals (flat quads), flames (billboards)

lighting.defaultNote: the scene opens (and Play uses) this mood; the others are the lab's lighting presets of the same scene
lighting.lightsNote: lights[] are build-time values; the scene multiplies every candle / torch / kiln by moods[...].lightScale and flickers them (1/f noise); the bell spot is the one shadowed light
